items.title: 1.9 Trends in bonding in the oxides and chlorides of period 3

source_refs.note: Topic 1.9, printed page 16, as printed: the ionic-to-covalent trend in period 3 oxides and chlorides.

blocks.text: Oxides of group 1, 2 & 3 (e.g., Na₂O) have more ionic character. These oxides exist as giant ionic lattices with strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions. Oxides of group 4, 5, 6 & 7 (e.g., SO₂) are more covalent. These oxides exist as covalent molecules with weak intermolecular forces. This transition is a result of the increasing electronegativity and decreasing ionic character.

Similar to oxides, chlorides of group 1, 2 and 3 (e.g., NaCl) are predominately ionic. Chlorides of elements from group 4, 5, 6 and 7 (e.g., PCl₅) are covalent. The covalent character in chlorides increases due to decrease in difference of electronegativity between the halogen and the other atom.
